card.title: Drop the Armor
card.instruction: Persuade someone to lower their guard, stop performing strength, or admit what affects them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Over dinner you keep saying you're managing. What's hard about going home?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The silence. I leave the television on so it sounds occupied.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you ask me over instead of pretending you've got company?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll cook. I promise I won't be miserable all evening.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you invite me without that promise? I'd like to come even if you're miserable and we eat toast.

mechanism: A encourages a lonely person to ask for real company without promising to be cheerful or impressive.
confusable: Unlike offering generic comfort, A must remove the performed-strength conditions B places on accepting it.
comparison: D108-b offers toast and misery as acceptable company; D108-a makes being off the clock a reason to drop the cheerful voice.
provenance: Direct local assistant candidate preparation; not fresh review or acceptance.
